proposals.before: the 44th year of Biography
proposals.after: Biography 44
proposals.reason: Chinese 列傳第四十四 is the biography serial number, not a year; the idiomatic English invents 'year'.

proposals.before: Empress Wang gave birth to the Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi and to Prince Dalian of Nankang.
proposals.after: Empress Wang gave birth to the Lamented Crown Prince Daqi and to Prince Dalian of Nanjun.
proposals.reason: 大器 is Daqi, not Dadqi; 南郡 is Nanjun (Nan Commandery), not Nankang (南康).

proposals.before: Empress Wang bore the Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi and Prince Dalian of Nankang.
proposals.after: Empress Wang bore the Lamented Crown Prince Daqi and Prince Dalian of Nanjun.
proposals.reason: Same errors as the idiomatic line: Dadqi for 大器 and Nankang for 南郡.

proposals.before: Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liyang.
proposals.after: Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liuyang.
proposals.reason: 瀏陽 is Liuyang, not Liyang (歷陽).

proposals.before: Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liyang.
proposals.after: Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liuyang.
proposals.reason: 瀏陽 is Liuyang, not Liyang.

proposals.before: Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dadjun of Xiyang.
proposals.after: Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dajun of Xiyang.
proposals.reason: 大鈞 is Dajun; Dadjun inserts an erroneous d.

proposals.before: Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dadjun of Xiyang.

proposals.before: Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Dadun, who died young and received no enfeoffment.
proposals.after: Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Daxun, who died young and received no enfeoffment.
proposals.reason: 大訓 is Daxun, not Dadun.

proposals.before: Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Dadun, who died young without a fief.
proposals.after: Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Daxun, who died young without a fief.
proposals.reason: 大訓 is Daxun, not Dadun.

proposals.before: In the third year the Terrace City fell; Xiao Shao of the superior armor fled south with a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and given the title General Who Pacifies the South.
proposals.after: In the third year the Terrace City fell; Marquis Xiao Shao of Shangjia fled south with a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and given the title General Who Pacifies the South.
proposals.reason: 上甲侯 is the noble title Marquis of Shangjia, not 'superior armor'.

proposals.before: In the third year the Terrace City fell; the superior armor officer Xiao Shao fled south bearing a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
proposals.after: In the third year the Terrace City fell; Marquis Xiao Shao of Shangjia fled south bearing a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
proposals.reason: 上甲侯 is Marquis of Shangjia, not a 'superior armor officer'.

proposals.before: At first, Zhuang Tie, Administrator of Liyang, surrendered the city to Hou Jing, but afterward he brought his mother and came over to Daxin.
proposals.after: At first, Zhuang Tie, Administrator of Liyang, surrendered the city to Hou Jing, but afterward he brought his mother and came over as a refugee.
proposals.reason: Chinese 來奔 means came fleeing or defecting and does not name Daxin as the destination.

proposals.before: Sizian, heir of Poyang, was Tie's friend and told Fan, "I used to keep company with Tie—he is clever and bold. If he surrenders to Jiangzhou they will not spare his life. Please aid him."
proposals.after: Si, the heir of Poyang, had previously been friendly with Tie and told Fan, "I used to keep company with Tie—he is clever and bold. If he surrenders to Jiangzhou they will not spare his life. Please aid him."
proposals.reason: Chinese 嗣 is the heir's given name and 先 means previously; 嗣先 is not a personal name Sizian.

proposals.before: The heir of Poyang, Sizian, was friendly with Tie and said to Fan, "In the past I associated with Tie; his talent and stratagems are resourceful—if he surrenders to Jiangzhou, his head will surely not be spared. Please rescue him."
proposals.after: The heir of Poyang, Si, was previously friendly with Tie and said to Fan, "In the past I associated with Tie; his talent and stratagems are resourceful—if he surrenders to Jiangzhou, his head will surely not be spared. Please rescue him."
proposals.reason: Chinese 嗣 is the personal name and 先 is the adverb previously, not part of the name.

proposals.before: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai commandery, went out as Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Dongyang, and was also removed to be Prefect of Wu commandery.
proposals.after: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai commandery, went out as Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Dongyang, and was also appointed Prefect of Wu commandery.
proposals.reason: Chinese 除 means to appoint to office, not to remove from office.

proposals.before: At the time Zhang Biao raised a righteous army in Kuaiji; the men of Wu, Lu Linggong and Yingchuan's Yu Mengqing, urged Dalin to join him.
proposals.after: At the time Zhang Biao raised a righteous army in Kuaiji; Lu Linggong of Wu and Yu Mengqing of Yingchuan urged Dalin to join him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 吳人 modifies only 陸令公; 潁川庾孟卿 is a separate native-place label.

proposals.before: and if he is crushed, to go because I urged it—that I will not do."
proposals.after: and if he is crushed and defeated, they would blame it on me—I must not go."
proposals.reason: Chinese 以我說焉 means the failure would be explained by reference to him, not that he goes because he urged it.

proposals.before: Prince Dalian of Nankang, styled Renjing, was the fifth son of Emperor Jianwen.
proposals.after: Prince Dalian of Nanjun, styled Renjing, was the fifth son of Emperor Jianwen.
proposals.reason: Chinese 南郡 is Nanjun, not Nankang; s0234 correctly renders the same title as Nanjun.

proposals.before: Prince Dalian of Nankang, style name Renjing, was Emperor Jianwen's fifth son.
proposals.after: Prince Dalian of Nanjun, style name Renjing, was Emperor Jianwen's fifth son.
proposals.reason: Chinese 南郡 is Nanjun, not Nankang; the same fief is translated Nanjun at s0234.

proposals.before: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu and made Inspector of Dongyang.
proposals.after: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu and made Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 東揚州 is Eastern Yangzhou, not Dongyang; s0228 correctly uses Eastern Yangzhou for the same office.

proposals.before: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu commandery and went out as Inspector of Dongyang.
proposals.after: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu commandery and went out as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 東揚州刺史 denotes Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, not Dongyang.

proposals.before: Duke Daya of Liyang, styled Renfeng, was the twelfth son of Emperor Jianwen.
proposals.after: Duke Daya of Liuyang, styled Renfeng, was the twelfth son of Emperor Jianwen.
proposals.reason: 瀏陽 is Liuyang; Liyang drops the medial u.

proposals.before: Duke Daya of Liyang, style name Renfeng, was Emperor Jianwen's twelfth son.
proposals.after: Duke Daya of Liuyang, style name Renfeng, was Emperor Jianwen's twelfth son.
proposals.reason: 瀏陽 is Liuyang.

proposals.before: In the ninth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang.
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Liuyang.
proposals.reason: 瀏陽 is Liuyang.

proposals.before: In the ninth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang county.
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Liuyang county.
proposals.reason: 瀏陽 is Liuyang.

proposals.before: Prince Dadjun of Xiyang, styled Renbo, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
proposals.after: Prince Dajun of Xiyang, styled Renbo, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
proposals.reason: 大鈞 is Dajun; Dadjun inserts an erroneous d.

proposals.after: Prince Dajun of Xiyang, style name Renbo, was Emperor Jianwen's fourteenth son.
proposals.reason: 大鈞 is Dajun, not Dadjun.

proposals.before: The imperial son Dadun, styled Rende, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
proposals.after: The imperial son Daxun, styled Rende, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
proposals.reason: 大訓 is Daxun; Dadun confuses 訓 (xun) with dun.

proposals.before: The imperial son Dadun, style name Rende, was Emperor Jianwen's sixteenth son.
proposals.after: The imperial son Daxun, style name Rende, was Emperor Jianwen's sixteenth son.
proposals.reason: 大訓 is Daxun, not Dadun.

proposals.before: He then worshiped the Buddha at the six hours and likewise said, "Whatever living beings ought to receive the report of suffering, let Daqiu take it all."
proposals.after: He then worshiped the Buddha at the six hours and likewise said, "Whatever living beings ought to receive the retribution of suffering, let Daqiu take it all."
proposals.reason: 苦報 means karmic retribution of suffering, not a report.

proposals.before: In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master with Opens Office and Parallels in Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
proposals.after: In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master Unequaled in Ceremonial with the Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
proposals.reason: Opens Office is a calque of 開府 that obscures 開府儀同三司; use the conventional English office name.

proposals.before: In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master with Opens Office and Parallels in Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
proposals.after: In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master Unequaled in Ceremonial with the Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
proposals.reason: Same calque of 開府 as Opens Office in the literal rendering.

proposals.before: The Martial and Fierce heir, with talent fit to stem disaster, held the charge of the heir in the tomb-line—yet in the end he was cast aside that same year; fortune and misfortune, too, are said to be fate. Alas!
proposals.after: The Martial and Fierce heir, with talent fit to manage his father's unfinished work, held the charge of the primary heir—yet in the end he was cast aside that same year; fortune and misfortune, too, are said to be fate. Alas!
proposals.reason: 塚嗣 means the designated primary heir of the ancestral line, not a literal tomb-line; 幹蠱 means managing the father's unfinished affairs.

decisions.reason: s0001 列傳第四十四 is the biography serial number; the idiomatic 'year' is invented and Biography 44 matches the Chinese.
s0004 哀太子大器、南郡王大連: 大器 is Daqi and 南郡 is Nanjun; Dadqi and Nankang are wrong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 哀太子大器、南郡王大連

decisions.reason: Literal of s0004 repeats Dadqi for 大器 and Nankang for 南郡; Daqi and Nanjun are correct.
s0007 瀏陽公大雅: 瀏陽 is Liuyang, not Liyang (歷陽).
Literal likewise misreads 瀏陽 as Liyang; Liuyang is the accurate place-name.
s0009 西陽王大鈞: 大鈞 is Dajun; Dadjun inserts a spurious d.
Literal of s0009 has the same Dadjun error for 大鈞; Dajun is correct.
s0015 皇子大訓: 大訓 is Daxun, not Dadun.
Literal likewise misreads 大訓 as Dadun; Daxun matches the Chinese.
s0054 上甲侯蕭韶: 上甲侯 is Marquis of Shangjia, not 'superior armor'.
Literal of s0054 likewise misreads 上甲侯 as a superior-armor office; Marquis of Shangjia is correct.
s0056 奉其母來奔 states only that he came fleeing/defecting; naming Daxin as destination is not in the Chinese.
s0062 鄱陽世子嗣先與鐵善: 嗣 is the heir's name and 先 means previously; Sizian is a false compound.
Literal of s0062 likewise treats 嗣先 as one name; Si plus adverb 先 is the correct parse.

decisions.after: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai commandery, went out as Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, and was also appointed Prefect of Wu commandery.
decisions.reason: s0082 又除吳郡太守: 除 means appoint, so 'removed' is wrong; the proposal still leaves 東揚州 as Dongyang, which must be Eastern Yangzhou.

s0134 西陽王大鈞: 大鈞 is Dajun; Dadjun is wrong.
